briefing_title_en: Daily Briefing: AI Agents, Sudan Strikes and Market Crosscurrents
briefing_summary_en: This briefing covers seven sections and 57 final articles. AI coverage focuses on cowork agents, procedural memory and clinical reliability research; OpenAI says it will add Orchestra Bio's team and technology to Rosalind, while Anthropic's safety bill is reported to require a judge's permission before blocking a release. Developer items cover Copilot practice and the eMudhra intermediate CA key compromise. Internationally, sources say Sudanese army drone strikes killed more than 300 people, Nigeria confirmed an Ebola case, and about 76% of Alberta voters rejected independence. China reports climate and carbon-market progress and launched the first Wuyang satellite. Markets rose on tech earnings that eased AI-trade concerns; oil gained on Hormuz attacks and falling inventories, while BOJ rate-hike expectations remain a former official's forecast.

articles.title: SPEM：面向 LLM 智能体高效技能使用的结构感知程序记忆

sections.briefing_title_en: AI & LLMs Daily: Agent Training and Evaluation, OpenAI Biotech Acquisition, and Safety Governance
sections.briefing_summary_en: This edition covers five frontier-model papers: Navalia uses verifiable task synthesis and long-horizon post-training for cowork agents; industrial agentic AI examines LLM agents’ autonomous planning and deployment barriers in smart manufacturing; AtomSD and SPEM improve agents’ skill use through procedural atom-guided self-distillation and structure-aware procedural memory; and another study analyzes transformer inference via high-dimensional layer-state trajectories. On the product side, OpenAI is folding Orchestra Bio’s team and technology into Rosalind and Rosalind Workbench. Research and governance items include MAMath-Bench for multimodal multi-agent math reasoning, Anthropic’s proposed AI safety bill, a study on multi-agent collaboration and clinical hallucination, CERTA’s decision-level certification for clinical models, and WaveCommitments for speech-agent marketplaces.

subsections.briefing_summary: 先进成像研究显示，他汀可附着于肌肉细胞中的关键蛋白并迫使其打开，从而解释部分患者为何出现肌痛、无力乃至严重肌损伤。新研究还发现，改进后的飓风预报图有助于识别受威胁区域，却未必提升风险认知或促使防护行动，“飓风锥”误解仍存。研究人员在怀俄明州约1.6亿年前地层识别出已知最“胖”的箭石，一种桶状鱿鱼近亲，显示前所未见的形态并可能是小型头足类捕食者。另一项小鼠研究中，阻断参与神经元破坏的免疫细胞可减轻阿尔茨海默病相关脑损伤，即使未清除有害tau蛋白，记忆中心组织仍多保留约40%，记忆也有改善。
subsections.briefing_title_en: Statin Muscle Pain, Hurricane Warnings, Jurassic Fossil and Alzheimer’s Research
subsections.briefing_summary_en: Advanced imaging shows statins can attach to a crucial muscle-cell protein and force it open, explaining why some patients develop muscle pain, weakness or severe damage. A new study finds improved hurricane forecast graphics help identify threatened areas but do not necessarily increase perceived danger or protective action, and misunderstanding of the hurricane cone persists. In Wyoming, researchers identified the ‘fattest’ belemnite ever found—a barrel-shaped squid relative from about 160 million years ago—revealing a previously unknown form and a possible small cephalopod predator. In a mouse study, blocking immune cells involved in neuron destruction reduced Alzheimer’s-related brain damage; memory centers retained about 40% more tissue and memory improved even without removing toxic tau.
